newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Anxiety over Wall Street and weak local bonds weighed South African shares which finished weaker on Monday, dealers said.
But they added that local shares were holding up well in the wake of the Dow's 148-point plunge on Friday.

"Wall Street is still a bit uncertain and U.S. long bonds are looking weak too. They're seen easing to about 7.25 percent and if this happens there could be further uncertainty on U.S. stocks which will have a ruction down here," one dealer said.
The local market was seen waiting the overnight close of U.S. stocks, which were last more than 30 points down.

The U.S. CPI number due on Tuesday and the U.S. industrial production number due Wednesday were also causing jitters because, if inflationary, could knock U.S. stocks and then equity markets worldwide.
"Trade has been a little nervous ahead of U.S. numbers which if inflationary will see even more Wall Street uncertainty," a dealer said.
Dealers earlier said that talk had already started about the possibility of a further U.S. interest rate hike when the Federal Reserve meets again in May.
This was seen impacting on South African stocks via a rand which would fall on a stronger dollar.
But despite this week's trade seen against a backdrop of negative caution, local shares were seen continuing to hold their heads above water.
"Our market has held up pretty well so far and we have the benefit of things not looking too bad economically," a dealer said.
Overall trade was quiet though, adding to the indices' volatility. There were a number of large bookovers, including 152,000 Amcoal shares at 2.85 rand and three million Avis shares at seven rand.
"There was also quite a nice bookover in Anglo," one dealer said.
The all-share index fell 55.6 points to 6,966.4 and the industrial index shed 47.2 points to 8,166.8 points.
Gold shares shrank their value in sympathy with overall market caution, but they were depressed further by a lacklustre bullion price and upcoming first quarter gold results.

South African gold mines begin the first quarter round of reporting on Thursday. Results are seen hacked by the double whammy of a strong rand and weak bullion price in the first three months of this year.
The gold index was off 23.8 points at 1,283.
Vaal Reefs was off 11.50 rand at 278.50 rand and Gold Fields lost 300 cents to 107.50 rand.
Local futures opened sharply lower after the Dow's pummelling on Friday but recovered small ground by close.
The weaker rand and bond market eroded support.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,420/441 from Friday's 6,465, the industrial contract was down at 7,972/80 from 8,013 settlement. The gold contract was at 902/920 from 924.
-- Melanie Cheary, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
